requirement_text: You can enter by taking the TOL - Test on Line (provided by Politecnico di Milano), test administered in Italian, and/or one of the following alternative tests: TOLC-I (provided by the Consortium of Inter-University Integrated Access Systems - CISIA www.cisiaonline.it), test administered in Italian; CEnT-S (provided by the Consortium of Inter-University Integrated Access Systems - CISIA www.cisiaonline.it), test administered in English; SAT (provided by The College Board www.collegeboard.org), test administered in English.
researcher_notes: Per the research brief's specific instruction for Italy: recording the test name AND administering body for each option, not just a pass/fail threshold. Four distinct entrance-test routes for Engineering Laurea programmes, two administered by Politecnico itself (TOL) or the national CISIA consortium (TOLC-I/CEnT-S), one entirely external (SAT, College Board) -- genuinely different administering authorities for what functions as the same admission gate, exactly the centralised-but-multi-test national test structure the brief anticipated for Italy generally.

requirement_text: If you want to enrol in a course taught in Italian, you have to prove: proficiency in the Italian language, prior to enrolment. You can fulfil the language requirement, if you: are a citizen of either Italy or the Republic of San Marino or the Swiss Canton of Ticino [...]; or have a qualification, at least upper secondary school level, obtained in Italian [...]; or have an appropriate B2 level certification of proficiency in the Italian language issued by the CLIQ (Certificazione Lingua Italiana di Qualita). [...] Proficiency in English is not an entry requirement, but it is necessary to continue and complete your Laurea [...] programme. If you do not provide evidence of proficiency in English, you will be assigned the OFA ENG (additional educational obligations for English), which entails certain career limitations.
researcher_notes: For Italian-medium programmes: Italian B2 is an entry gate (citizenship/diploma/CLIQ cert), English is NOT an entry gate but its absence triggers 'OFA ENG' (obbligo formativo aggiuntivo / additional educational obligation) -- a deferred remedial requirement with real consequences ('certain career limitations') rather than a simple binary admission bar. This OFA mechanism is a genuinely different requirement shape from a pass/fail threshold and doesn't map cleanly onto either -- recorded descriptively rather than forced into a scalar.

requirement_text: In order to be admitted to Bachelor of Science programmes held in English, you must demonstrate: proficiency in English prior to enrolment. You can fulfil the language requirement, if you: are a citizen of a country where the official language is English [...]; or have a qualification, at least upper secondary school level, obtained in English [...]; have an appropriate certification of English language proficiency as specified on the Web page [...]. Proficiency in Italian is not an entry requirement, but you will need to obtain a B2 level in Italian before completing your Bachelor of Science programme. You can demonstrate proficiency in the Italian language if you: take a TOL or TOLC-I with a score of at least 30/100; are a citizen of either Italy or the Republic of San Marino or the Swiss Canton of Ticino; have a qualification, at least upper secondary school level, obtained in Italian. If you do not demonstrate proficiency in Italian, you will be assigned the OFA (additional educational obligation) for Italian.
researcher_notes: Mirror-image structure to the Italian-track record above: for English-medium programmes, English proficiency is the entry gate and Italian becomes the deferred OFA obligation instead -- notably, one concrete numeric threshold IS given here for the Italian side: a TOL or TOLC-I score of at least 30/100 satisfies the B2-equivalent Italian requirement for graduation, a genuinely scalar sub-fact within an otherwise non-scalar OFA structure.
